The Earth has been warming up since the last ice age. But it was doing it very slowly. Now, it's starting to warm up faster. Primarily because humanity is pumping tons of green house gases (gases that retain heat well) into the atmosphere. Specifically, CO2 (Carbon Dioxide).

As the Sun's rays hit the Earth, it warms the Earth up. Some of the heat is usually radiated back into space, among other things, but more green house gases means less heat will leave Earth and so the Earth will get hotter.

As this has happened, the Earth has gotten hotter, faster than it was before. The Earth has systems in place to manage the heat. To take heat in a place where it's too hot and put it where there's less heat. Specifically, the ocean and the wind.

The ocean is massive and is made up primarily of water. Water has a very high thermal capacity. Much higher than air. It also is a better thermal conductor, meaning it moves heat better than air. That means that a small amount of water can hold a lot of heat and move it quickly.

So, the largest amount of water on the planet is heating up. That requires a ton of heat, which means things are getting worse, but we aren't directly seeing the effects of it because we don't live in the ocean. We see some of the effects, but only some.

The first thing that's going to heat up as the Earth gets hotter and hotter is the Ocean, because it manages the majority of the heat and it's the largest thing to hold the heat we have.

Note that when I say hotter, I mean like 1-3 Celsius hotter, but that's not good at all. The amount needed to start melting the aforementioned methane at the bottom of the ocean is only like 3-5C, and once it starts, it'd be very hard to stop happening (it's a cycle that feeds into itself making things worse).

And don't think "Oh, well, things will be fine. They always are." We already screwed to a point. The best we could do is mitigate Climate Change's effects. Stopping it isn't an option anymore.

We aren't past the point of no return, but we are to the point where many will die. Too much heat means not enough food (imagine what will happen to our agriculture as ecosystems change).

Personally I am a bit wary of these findings for the same reasons I assert that balding hair is negligible in an evolutionary sense. Most men don't start balding until their forties or above. When you think about it, evolution should and does only select favorable traits that express themselves through and up to when its host has sex and bears a child.
